clues: This city sits on the south bank of a big river in the South, close to the center of its state. Flat delta land gives way to low hills just west of here.
Summers here are hot and sticky, and winters are cool with hardly any snow. Yet the heat has hit 114, and the cold has sunk to 12 below zero.
The seat of rule moved to this river town in 1821, from a post that kept flooding. It has stayed here ever since that move.
A French explorer in 1722 named this place for a low stone ledge on the river bank. Boat crews used that ledge as a landmark as they passed.
The governor of Arkansas works in this city. State lawmakers meet here, at the seat of state rule.
